questionText: How does Spring Boot serialize and deserialize JSON with Jackson?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can trace a JSON request through Spring MVC and Jackson into a DTO, then trace a returned DTO back to a negotiated JSON response.
prerequisites: Java records or simple DTO classes

claims.statement: Spring MVC resolves an @RequestBody parameter by reading the HTTP request body through a suitable HttpMessageConverter for the declared Java type.
A Jackson-backed Spring MVC message converter can read JSON into the declared Java type and write a returned Java value as JSON using the application's configured mapper.
When @Valid is applied to an @RequestBody parameter, Bean Validation evaluates the object after successful message conversion rather than validating malformed JSON bytes directly.
Content-Type identifies the representation sent in a message, while Accept communicates which response media types a client prefers.

examples.title: Compile the learner controller and verify request and response JSON with MockMvc

validation.command: Run mvn -q test with Java 17 in an isolated Spring Boot 3.3.1 fixture containing the learner controller and a focused MockMvc request
validation.expected: Posting display_name Ada as application/json reaches the DTO and the returned response JSON contains id 42 and displayName Ada

visuals.title: A linear request-to-response path with separate read-side and write-side Jackson converters

notes: The revised diagram does not reuse one mapper node in a way that visually creates an accidental response-to-request path.
The learner code is deliberately small, while the evidence fixture supplies the MockMvc setup needed to prove both conversion directions.

review.notes: Spring MVC conversion and validation behavior was checked against official Spring Framework and Spring Boot 3.3.1 documentation, and media semantics against RFC 9110. The Java 17 Spring Boot 3.3.1 MockMvc fixture passed.
